title: Spelling Teams: oo
goal: I can spell words with oo, like moon and book.

card.desc: Bristol learns that the oo team says two sounds: the moon sound (moon, food, spoon, school, zoo) and the book sound (book, look, good, foot, cook, wood). Both are spelled with two o's. She sorts oo words by sound with word cards and fixes her spelling of bock for book. It is her first lesson after the winter break, on Zoom, so it opens with her Holiday Gazette pages.

win: Wow! The oo team is on your side too! 🌙📖

teacher.objective: Bristol learns that the oo team says two sounds, the moon sound (moon, food, spoon, school, zoo) and the book sound (book, look, good, foot, cook, wood), and that both are spelled with two o's. She sorts oo words by sound, tells oo from a short o (hot, dog, box), and fixes her bock-for-book spelling. Week 7 Day 2 (Practice it). Her first lesson after the winter break, on Zoom: it opens with a short welcome back (her Holiday Gazette pages and a quick remember check of ea).
materials: Zoom with screen share (open the Class lesson from the course page, code 9110)
At her home (ask Tia to write them before the lesson): 10 index cards: moon, food, pool, zoo, tooth, book, look, foot, wood, cook
At her home: paper or a small whiteboard and a marker; she holds her writing up to the camera. Your own whiteboard to hold up too.
A small mirror at her home (optional, for round lips on the moon sound)
Her Holiday Gazette pages (River's Diary and her Tray Math), next to the computer
Packet (2 pages) for Tia to print this week (it is on Wednesday's line of the task list)

plan.do: Class slide 1. Share your screen. Welcome her back. Check that Tia set out the cards, paper and her Gazette pages. Quick remember check: What does ea say?
Class slide 2. She holds her pages up to the camera, reads River's Diary and shows her Tray Math. You are the audience. Praise one true thing.
Class slide 3. Trimmed to 3 minutes for the welcome back. What she read over the break; an ea word and an oo word from her book.
Class slide 4. Trimmed to 2 minutes. Check her Lesson 16 After-Class score and her break work first. She says each answer; you type.
Class slide 5. The moon sound and the book sound.
Class slides 6–7. She reads and spells each word.
Class slide 8. She reads each word out loud and names the box; you tap.
Class slide 9. She writes bock on her paper, crosses it out, writes book, and holds it up.
Class slide 10. Short o (hot, pot) vs. the oo team.
Class slide 11. Two piles at home, held up to the camera; act out a word; a silly sentence.
Class slide 12. She reads every choice before she tells you her pick.
Class slides 13–14. Paper first, held up to the camera; then she spells and you type.
Class slide 15. She reads, copies and underlines the oo words, then holds up her paper.
Class slide 16. On her own. She says; you type.
Class slide 17. Show the task list: tonight the After-Class Lesson and 10 minutes of reading; the rest on Tuesday night and Wednesday. Lesson 18 is Tuesday, in person.

watch: bock for book (her own mistake), lok for look, mon for moon: one o. Ask: "Moon sound or book sound? Then it needs two o's."
u for the oo sounds (fud, gud, skool, spune). Say: "This week, that sound is spelled oo."
school spelled skool or scool. It is a word to remember: s-c-h-o-o-l.
Sorting by looks instead of sound. Have her say each word next to moon and next to book.
Some words sound different in different places (roof, room, root, broom). We do not sort these by sound in this lesson. If she says a word another way, accept her way.
Words like door and floor if she finds them. Say: "That is a different sound. We learn it later."

packet_key.answer: Any 2 oo words from her book, spelled right, each marked moon or book correctly.

teacher.notes: This is her first lesson after the winter break, on Zoom, so it opens with a short welcome back: her Holiday Gazette pages (River's Diary and her Tray Math), about 4 minutes, held up to the camera, and a quick remember check of ea. To keep the class at 60 minutes, the Book Talk is trimmed from 6 to 3 minutes and Recall from 3 to 2. Tonight is light: the After-Class Lesson and 10 minutes of reading. The Practice and page 2 of the Lesson 16 Packet are on Tuesday night; this Packet and the reading lesson on Wednesday. Lesson 18 (Tuesday, in person) is Prove it: ea and oo mixed, and a spelling list Tia reads aloud in the packet. Ask her to bring the 10 oo cards. If she scores under 85 on Show What You Know, she does 5 minutes of card piles with Tia (moon pile and book pile) and retakes it (new set) before Tuesday; if she is still under 85, start Lesson 18 with the card piles on the table.

tasks: Monday night: do the After-Class Lesson. Finish with Show What You Know.
Monday night: read your book for 10 minutes.
Tuesday night: do the Lesson 17 Practice. Try to get 85 or more. Then do page 2 of the Lesson 16 Packet (the page you saved).
Wednesday: do the Lesson 17 Packet, pages 1 and 2.
Wednesday: do the reading lesson Reading Foundations: oo. Read words with oo, like moon and book. Aim for 90. If it is locked, type 1111.
Lesson 18 is Tuesday, in person. Bring your book and your oo cards.

slides.title: Welcome Back: Spelling Teams: oo
slides.text: Welcome back from your break! 🎉 First, show your Holiday Gazette. Then meet a new team: the oo team can say two sounds! 🌙📖

notes.do: Share your screen. Before the lesson, ask Tia to set out, next to her: 10 index cards (moon, food, pool, zoo, tooth, book, look, foot, wood, cook), paper or a small whiteboard and a marker, a small mirror if she has one, her book, and her Holiday Gazette pages.
notes.say: "Welcome back! Before the break you learned the ea team. First, your Holiday Gazette. Then the oo team. It is a little tricky: it can say two sounds."
notes.ask: "What do you remember from before the break? What does the ea team usually say?"
notes.listen: Long e. This is your quick remember check: note anything she could not say.

slides.title: My Holiday Gazette
slides.text: Show your Gazette pages. Hold them up to the camera! 📰
prompts: Read River's Diary out loud. Hold it up to the camera.
Show your Tray Math. How many rows? How many in each row?
What was your favorite part of the Gazette? Why?

notes.do: About 4 minutes. You are the audience. She holds each page up to the camera, reads River's Diary (page 4) out loud, then shows her Tray Math from the Kitchen Corner.
notes.say: "Thank you for sharing your Gazette. You and your family worked hard on this over the break."
notes.ask: "Which part was your favorite? Why?" "How many rows were on the tray? How many in each row? So how many in all?"
notes.listen: She reads smoothly and holds the page still. Praise one true thing: a capital letter, a period, writing as River with I and my. On Tray Math, equal rows mean multiply (rows × how many in each row).

slides.title: Teams in my book
slides.text: Think about the book you are reading.
prompts: What happened in your book over the break?
Did you find an ea word? Long e or short e?
Find a word with oo in your book. Read it.

notes.do: About 3 minutes (trimmed for the welcome back). She holds the page up to the camera.
notes.ask: "What happened?" "Read me your ea word. Long or short e?" "Read me your oo word."
notes.listen: An ea word with the right sound. Write her oo word on your whiteboard; you will sort it later. If she finds door or floor, say: "That one has a different sound. We learn it later."

slides.text: oo is a vowel team too. It can say two sounds.

steps.text: 🌙 The moon sound. Say moon. Your lips make a small, round circle: ooo.

Say them both: mooon … book. Hear the difference?

notes.listen: moon is long and round; book is short and quick.
